chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If the one in Ihram plucks from the hair of his beard, or anything from other than it, then upon him is that he feeds a poor person in his hand.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.فِي يَدِهِ: In his hand (indicating the specific poor person chosen by the offender)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram plucking beard hair?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific fidyah (expiation) for plucking hair while in Ihram, prescribing the feeding of one poor person as compensation. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is often cited to demonstrate the principle of proportional expiation for minor violations of Ihram restrictions, distinguishing it from the heavier penalties associated with major prohibitions like cutting hair with shears.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If the one in Ihraam were to pluck from the hair of his beard, or anything from other than it, so upon him is that he feeds a poor one in his hand’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one in the state of Ihram pulls out a hair from his beard or from other parts of his body, he must feed one destitute person in his hand (with one meal).”’
